READY / security PASS

PR #245 at 6a52a0950d2be8f5e05908384b258144d5976e64.
Answers role:security/245 request 01a1f0ff-6664-7c32-bf2f-6636fbd907b7.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No security vulnerabilities found | - |

Authority: an unauthorized initial close returns before scheduling
(crates/daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs:496-498). Each changed-row retry rereads
the target, checks incarnation and tombstone state, and rechecks the caller's
authority; an authority refusal terminates rather than retrying. Only Changed
retries (crates/daemon/src/http/memory_turn.rs:444-478). The descriptor CAS
compares the complete row within its write transaction
(crates/store/src/registry.rs:61-74). No new permission laundering found.

Memory-note attribution: the directory handler derives the caller and rejects
contradictory actor claims (crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:560-578);
memory.note is appended on that actor (1874-1890), not a selectable other seat.
Recognition queries the closing seat and checks project, held role, and the
newest holding-start timestamp (crates/daemon/src/http/memory_turn.rs:588-608).
Generic spine append also binds the seat to the resolved actor and cannot
supply the required role payload
(crates/daemon/src/http/governance.rs:1525-1548).
This preserves C33's user-account trust boundary, not a per-seat credential
guarantee.

Rendering: new structured fields are JSON-serialized. Memory INDEX titles
are Markdown-escaped (crates/daemon/src/community/memory.rs:451-492), the git
message is a separate process argument, not shell text
(crates/daemon/src/community/writer.rs:246-258), and tombstoned delivery
refusals fence the complete reason (crates/core/src/error.rs:115-120).
No new unsafe shell/path exposure or published secret found in the nine-file
diff.

Policy/brakes: the timeout bound and note-recognition rule are policies;
per-attempt incarnation, tombstone, and authority rechecks are brakes.
Cost qualification: a new bounded retry loop allows five total attempts,
not five retries. There is no new recurring timer, poll, or launch site.
The five target refreshes plus one added spine lookup do not count all I/O:
existing CAS, optional liveness checks, and successful receipt lookup remain.
This is source evidence, not a live fleet cost measurement.

Validation: just pr-freeze 245 passed twice, including immediately before
publication: remote heads agree, main base, CLEAN, all five latest checks pass.
Exact-head CI run 44420460614: check (22), check (24), rust-lint and rust-test
SUCCESS; run 44420460637: delivers SUCCESS. Rust summary: 2,504 passed,
six skipped. JUnit artifact 14482580728 confirms memory-turn 19/19,
directory 111/111 and lifecycle 6/6, including retry, reparenting, revive,
pending-close, note recognition and title escaping witnesses.

Limits: source plus Linux CI only. No local cargo build/test, full harness
checks, mutation run, macOS execution, or live fleet measurement was performed.
The correctness role separately owns the broader lifecycle verdict.

Harness feedback, non-blocking: difficulties - the local done gate rebuilds
Rust while this review requires CI-only build proof; named test receipts need
manual JUnit correlation. magicWand - a read-only pr-freeze review receipt
that includes head-bound CI job IDs and named JUnit witnesses. No product
source or tracked review-worktree files were changed.
